title: D-Latch
body:
An [[SR-Latch]] with the invalid state engineered away. Feed one data line $D$ to $S$ and
$\bar{D}$ to $R$, so $S$ and $R$ can never both be 1, and gate the pair with an enable
line $E$.

| E | D | $Q_{next}$ |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| 0 | × | $Q$ (hold) |
| 1 | 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 1 | 1 |

The D-latch is **level-triggered**, sometimes called *transparent*: while the enable is
high, $Q$ follows $D$ continuously. Wiggle $D$ during that window and the output wiggles
with it. That is the one fact worth memorising, because it is exactly what separates a
latch from a [[Flip-Flop]], which is edge-triggered and only samples $D$ at the instant
the clock changes.

Transparency is a problem when the latch's output feeds back into the logic computing its
own input: the value can race around the loop more than once in a single enable pulse. The
edge-triggered [[Flip-Flop]] is the fix, which is why real [[Synchronous]] designs are
built from flip-flops rather than latches.
